Dear colleges,

Need help to understand why when calculating the model with a mediator, 
the regression index is greater than 1. 

It seems this is the most elementary type of question, but I'm really confused and can't get out of here for days.


models$TEST <-"

scbrL ~ brint*KINT + brass*KASS + brsep*KSEP 

scaL ~ s1*scboL + s2*scbrL
paL ~ p1*scboL + p2*scbrL

# residual correlations
KINT ~~ KASS
KINT ~~ KSEP
KASS ~~ KSEP
paL ~~ scaL

# Indirect

scbrint := s2*brint
scboint := s1*boint

scbrass := s2*brass

pbrint := p2*brint

pbrass := p2*brass

"

messages.subject: Re: Don't understand why St. Regression is higher than 1
parts:
Need help to understand why when calculating the model with a mediator, 
the regression index is greater than 1.

Why would this be a problem?  Are you thinking of the standardized regression coefficient (in the last column) not exceeding 1?  Because even that is not necessarily the case when you have multiple predictors.

https://www.researchgate.net/post/In_a_multiple_regression_analysis_can_the_beta_coefficient_be_larger_than_1_and_if_so_is_there_something_wrong_in_the_analysis
